claim: The BDE database domain is capped at heavy-atom count 10 (max over 42577 unique molecules) and contains only C, N and O; of the 543 benchmark observations, exactly 331 have an exact (molecule,fragment1,fragment2) row in the database, 369/543 have their parent molecule present, and 150/543 (27.6%) lie beyond the database HAC maximum of 10.
value_found: HAC max = 10 (min 1, mean 8.8915, over 42577 unique parent molecules; identical max 10 over 290664 unique (mol,f1,f2) pairs and over 484907 raw rows); heavy-atom elements = {C,N,O} (C 42577, N 26511, O 31558 unique molecules); exact rows = 331/543 (fragment-order swap adds 0; stereo-insensitive join also 331); parent molecule present = 369/543; HAC > 10 = 150/543 = 27.6243% (carried by 141 unique molecules, none of which appear in the DB). All five numbers match the reported values exactly.
unit: Three units checked separately and reported distinctly: (1) unique parent molecule (42577 in DB, 419 in benchmark) for HAC max and element set, also cross-checked over 290664 unique (molecule,fragment1,fragment2) triples and over all 484907 raw rows; (2) bond observation (543 benchmark rows) for the 331/369/150 coverage counts, with the 150 also confirmed as 141 unique molecules via groupby; (3) unique fragment (206797 pooled SMILES) for the element check. No unit substitution was found.
method: python3 -u /data/user/conversations/conv-75e3fc1d-c4c9-41b5-800b-05f4632eec99/project/output/analysis/verify_2_coverage.py  (log: output/logs/verify_2_run.log); second independent pass python3 -u output/analysis/verify_2_crosschecks.py (log: output/logs/verify_2_crosschecks.log). Own loaders (pandas.read_csv directly on the TSV and gz CSV), own RDKit feature cache; no import of common.py or any ws*.py. Cross-methods: RDKit GetNumHeavyAtoms vs rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula heavy-atom count (0 per-molecule mismatches, max 10 both ways) vs a regex raw-SMILES element scan; set-membership join vs pandas merge(how='left', indicator=True) (both give 331 and 369); row filter vs vectorised Series compare vs groupby-aggregation for the 150 (all agree). SHA256 of the TSV and DB match data_manifest.json.
notes: No discrepancy on any of the five numbers. Adversarial checks and residual caveats: (a) The 331/543 exact-row count uses the stored (molecule,fragment_a,fragment_b) orientation; swapping fragment_a/fragment_b adds exactly 0 matches, and a stereo-insensitive join (stripping / \ @) also stays 331, so the count is robust to those two plausible alternative join definitions. (b) 'Contains only C, N and O' is true of heavy atoms but NOT of all atoms: one fragment species is the bare hydrogen radical [H] (361147 fragment cells), and 14480 unique parent SMILES carry explicit-H tokens in the raw string (RDKit still reports 0 explicit H atoms in any parent graph). If read as an all-atom statement the claim is false; under the standard heavy-atom convention (the sentence itself is about heavy-atom count) it is exact. (c) The DB HAC cap is real but heavily piled up: 16373/42577 (38.5%) unique molecules sit exactly at HAC 10 and 69.9% at HAC >= 9, i.e. the cap is a dataset boundary, not an isolated maximum. (d) The 150 beyond-cap observations are carried by 141 unique molecules, and 0 of those 141 parents appear anywhere in the DB (parent-present = 0, exact-row = 0 among them), so the 'beyond the boundary' label is unambiguous at both the observation and molecule unit. (e) Sensitivity: the boundary count is cutoff-sensitive (HAC>9: 193, >10: 150, >11: 136), but 10 is the correct DB maximum under every definition tested. (f) Supplemental checks requested by the harness: CLAIM 5 - both methods agree, method A sigma_ref = 2.8437 (sd ddof=1 of E_i-E_j over 1002 pairs with |dQ| <= 0.1, divided by sqrt(2)); a variant using RMS instead of sample SD gives 2.8539; method B moment decomposition sqrt([V(E-Q)+V(E-L)-V(Q-L)]/2) = 2.8330 with V terms 9.0708/12.0191/5.0377; implied oracle MAE = 2.8330*sqrt(2/pi) = 2.2604. CLAIM 11 - correct pooled within-molecule SD = 9.9654 (variance 99.3086, SSw 12314.2718, df 124 from 86 multi-row molecules covering 210 observations; mean spread 13.4186, median 11.90, max 47.90 all reproduced). YES, a naive pooled-variance formula can produce the wrong ~165: sqrt( sum_i (n_i-1)*var_i^2 / sum_i (n_i-1) ) = 165.2623 exactly, i.e. pooling the SQUARED variances (var_i^2) instead of var_i under sqrt; other naive variants give 10.32, 10.11, 6.29 or 95.66, so the ~165 figure is specifically the squared-variance pooling error and the correct value is 9.97.
